title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 116
paragraphs: So when the herdsman had made the truth known, Astyages now cared less about him, but with Harpagos he was greatly displeased and ordered his spearmen to summon him. When Harpagos came, Astyages asked him thus: “By what death, Harpagos, did you destroy the child whom I delivered to you, born of my daughter?” Harpagos, seeing that the herdsman was in the king's palace, did not turn to any false way of speech, lest he be convicted and found out, but said as follows: “O king, as soon as I received the child, I took counsel and considered how I should act according to your wishes, and how, without offending your command, I might not be guilty of murder against your daughter and yourself. I therefore did this: I called this herdsman and delivered the child to him, telling him first that you were the one who ordered it to be killed — and in this at least I did not lie, for you did so command. I gave it to this man with instructions to place it on a desolate mountain, and to stay beside it and watch until it died, threatening him with every kind of punishment if he failed. And when he had done what was ordered and the child was dead, I sent the most trusted of my eunuchs and through them saw it and buried it. Thus, O king, it happened in this matter, and the child had the death I have described.”
